papers.title: Energy-Proportional Serverless Computing on SBC Clusters
authors: Yuliya Sasinskaya, Natalie Carl, Niklas Kowallik, David Bermbach
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.14026v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Serverless computing promises to run code only on demand, yet the servers beneath it draw most of their power while idle, so energy consumption does not scale to zero with the workload. We show that the statelessness of serverless functions makes it possible to extend scale-to-zero from function instances to physical nodes, enabling energy proportionality. Our platform, built on tinyFaaS for clusters of single-board computers, treats node power state as part of worker selection, powering workers off when idle and back on under load. On a physical cluster, our approach reduces mean power draw by 39.6 % on a bursty, trace-based workload and by 46.7 % on a sparse one, without a detectable change in median latency on the bursty workload. papers.title: Reconciling Strict SLOs with Low Cost under Fine-Grained Load Fluctuations
authors: Dilina Dehigama, Shyam Jesalpura, Zeyu Xu, Marton Nemeth, Shengda Zhu, Marios Kogias, Boris Grot
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2606.30533v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Cloud-based online services face significant sub-second load fluctuations while needing to meet strict Service Level Objectives (SLOs). Cluster operators often over-provision resources to protect SLOs, sacrificing utilization and cost efficiency. Existing reactive and proactive autoscalers, serverless (FaaS) deployments, and VM/FaaS hybrid systems fail to reconcile strict SLO compliance with low cost and high utilization under fine-grained load fluctuation.
